title: Throughput Validation Sandbox: Empirical Load Harness, Benchmark Methodology, and Customer Acceptance Checklist
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reproducible, tenant-aware sandbox and test harness to empirically validate Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees across latency and sustained throughput SLOs. This ticket covers the harness implementation, canonical benchmark recipes (including edge-case and mixed-tenant scenarios), telemetry capture format, and a customer acceptance checklist that maps measured artifacts to contractual guarantees.
objective: Deliver an easy-to-run test harness and a set of benchmark recipes that product/solutions can use during Dedicated onboarding to demonstrate that committed throughput and tail-latency targets are achievable under realistic tenant mixes and autoscaler behavior.
success_metrics: Reproducible end-to-end benchmark that produces token/sec, p50/p90/p99 latency, and error-rate artifacts
Automated check that validates >= 95% of sustained throughput target across 10m windows for standard tenant mixes
Customer-facing acceptance document with actionable run instructions and example telemetry
CI job that runs smoke load and fails PRs that degrade baseline throughput by >5%
experiment_matrix: Tenant mixes: single-tenant steady, multi-tenant 1:10 heavy/light, spike-heavy 90:10
Batching knobs: continuous batching ON/OFF, max_batch_size 8/32/64, prefetch window 0/50ms/200ms
Autoscaler policies: scale-to-zero disabled, aggressive (scale at 60% util), conservative (scale at 85% util), cooldown windows 30s/5m
KV cache hit/miss ratios: warm-cache 90%, cold-cache 10%, mixed 50%
Model variants: full-precision, 4-bit quantized, kernel-optimized variant
harness_components: Traffic generator (k8s job) with pluggable tenant profiles and request pacing
Scenario driver to stitch ramps, sustained phases, and microbursts into a single run
Telemetry collector that emits unified JSON artifacts: per-route token/sec, latency quantiles, CPU/GPU utilization, queue length
Replayer tool to convert customer production traces into deterministic harness inputs
Result aggregator that normalizes runs and produces comparison diff reports and flamegraphs for tail latency
benchmark_recipes: Onboarding baseline: 20m ramp, 30m sustain at committed throughput, 10m cool-down; report p50/p90/p99 and sustained token/sec
Microburst tolerance: 2m steady, 1m microburst at 2x committed than sustain, observe autoscaler response and error spike
Cold-start resilience: deploy new model variant with empty KV cache and run 30m replay to measure transient cost and latency
Mixed-tenant fidelity: simulate 50 tenants with heavy tail traffic distribution and measure fairness and QoS degradation
Autoscaler safety net: force node loss and validate fallback routing to spare capacity and no customer-facing errors
customer_acceptance_checklist: Run harness using 'onboarding baseline' recipe and attach aggregated JSON artifacts to ticket
Sustained throughput: measured sustained token/sec >= committed throughput - 5% for 90% of sampling windows
Tail SLOs: p99 latency <= contractual p99 + 10% for no more than 5 minutes during deployment windows
Error budget: request error-rate < 0.1% during sustain phase
Autoscaler behavior: documented scale-up time, scale-down cooldown, and observed max burst handling
Reproducibility: rerun by solutions engineer in different AZ and results within 3% of baseline
Artifacts: upload harness run ID, consolidated telemetry JSON, and comparison diff to customer-facing acceptance doc
tasks: Design harness API and telemetry schema (Aisha)
Implement tenant profile library and traffic generator (Ravi)
Integrate with CI and add baseline job (SRE)
Author benchmark recipes and example run logs (PM + Solutions)
Validate against staging Dedicated fleet and collect artifacts (QA)
Create customer-facing acceptance doc and onboarding checklist (Solutions)
Postmortem template and incident hooks for runs that exceed error budgets (Reliability)
notes: Trade-offs: prefer deterministic replay over synthetic randomness for customer acceptance to improve reproducibility
We will initially support only HTTP/gRPC generator; support for streaming websocket clients is scoped for follow-up
Telemetry format aligns with console-2025.02 cost/latency schema to allow direct upload to Console dashboards
Consider adding optional GPU-level tracing if deeper kernel-level diagnosis is required (follow-up ticket)
Benchmarks must include a 'no-quantization' and 'quantized' run for each model to expose quality/cost trade-offs
